title: When brain networks crash: connectivity, slow-wave activity and neural replay in Alzheimer's disease
title_zh: 脑网络崩溃时：阿尔茨海默病中的连通性、慢波活动与神经重放
abstract: Brain connectivity disruption is a hallmark of neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet how network breakdown gives rise to cognitive deficits remains unclear. Here, we review the evidence bearing on three interconnected processes that have been proposed to link molecular pathology to cognitive decline. First, we summarize evidence that misfolded proteins propagate along brain connectivity pathways, making the connectome the biological substrate for disease progression. Second, we discuss the divergent trajectory reported across the AD continuum, an initial compensatory hyperconnectivity followed by progressive hypoconnectivity and network collapse, together with the accompanying oscillatory changes (intrusion of slow-wave activity and suppression of fast oscillatory rhythms). Third, we examine the proposal that these oscillatory alterations compromise neural replay mechanisms, critical for memory consolidation, representing the potential link between network dysfunction and cognitive decline. By integrating evidence from human neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and animal models in the AD field, this framework offers new perspectives for therapeutic interventions targeting brain connectivity and replay mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract_zh: 脑连通性破坏是神经退行性疾病的标志，包括阿尔茨海默病（AD），但网络崩溃如何导致认知缺陷仍不清楚。本文综述了三种相互关联的过程的证据，这些过程被提出以连接分子病理与认知衰退。首先，总结了错误折叠蛋白沿脑连通通路传播的证据，使连接组成为疾病进展的生物学基础。其次，讨论了在AD连续体中报告的不同轨迹：最初的补偿性超连通性，随后是逐步的低连通性和网络崩溃，以及伴随的振荡变化（慢波活动的侵入和快速振荡节律的抑制）。第三，探讨了这些振荡改变如何破坏神经重放机制，后者对记忆巩固至关重要，可能是网络功能障碍与认知衰退之间的潜在联系。通过整合人类神经影像学、电生理学和动物模型的证据，该框架为针对脑连通性和重放机制的神经退行性疾病治疗干预提供了新的视角。
